To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CRP gene polymorphisms rs1205, rs2794521, rs2794539, and rs1800947 are significantly associated with CVD mortality, and that the rs1205 polymorphism is significantly associated with all-cause mortality in patients with IP.
the CRP gene polymorphisms were not predictive of cardiovascular disease (CVA) mortality in inflammatory polyarthitis.

understanding the genetic basis of CVD risk in patients with RA and IP.
the investigation of genetic polymorphisms of CRP gene as predictors of CVD mortality in patients with RA and IP.
the investigation of the genetic factors which may contribute to the increased cardiovascular mortality in patients with RA.

there is no evidence to support the use of C reactive protein as a screening tool in the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease.
the evidence for the use of CRP in the management of patients with RA is limited and should not be used to guide therapy at this time.
